Title: MRI of the liver and the pituitary gland in patients with beta-thalassemia major: does hepatic siderosis predict pituitary iron deposition?
Data_source_str: primary data
case_group_definition: patients with transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia major

Comparison Groups: Patients with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (group 1, n=13) vs those without pituitary dysfunction (group 2, n=13)
Clinical Outcome: Pituitary iron deposition (pituitary T2 and P/F)
Effect Value: r=-0.55 with L/F; r=-0.53 with pituitary T2; r=-0.55 with P/F

Title: Anti-factor VIII IgA as a potential marker of poor prognosis in acquired hemophilia A: results from the GTH-AH 01/2010 study.
Data_source_str: GTH-AH 01/2010 study
case_group_definition: patients with acquired hemophilia A (FVIII activity <50 IU/dL and inhibitor ≥0.6 BU/mL) enrolled within 7 days after starting immunosuppressive treatment
Study Population: 81 patients with AHA from GTH-AH 01/2010 study
Experimental Method Details: Fully validated semiquantitative direct binding ELISA for detection of FVIII-binding antibodies, including screening and titer determination; competition-based affinity ELISA for apparent affinities
Comparison Groups: Anti-FVIII IgA-positive vs anti-FVIII IgA-negative patients
Multivariable Result: Anti-FVIII IgA was the strongest negative predictor of recurrence-free survival after achieving partial remission and remained significant after adjustment for baseline demographic and clinical characteristics.
Evidence Quote: Anti-FVIII IgA-positive patients achieved partial remission similar to anti-FVIII IgA-negative patients but had a higher risk of subsequent recurrence. Consequently, IgA-positive patients achieved complete remission less frequently (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 0.35; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.18-0.68; P < .01) and had a higher risk of death (aHR, 2.62; 95% CI, 1.11-6.22; P < .05).

Title: The effects of hydroxyurea and bone marrow transplant on Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels in females with sickle cell anemia.
Data_source_str: SCA clinic or Ex-sickle-BMT clinic in the Aflac Cancer and Blood Disorders Center of Children's Healthcare of Atlanta
case_group_definition: Female subjects with sickle cell anemia (hemoglobin SS or hemoglobin Sβ0 thalassemia) aged 10-21 years, grouped by treatment: supportive care (SCA-SC), hydroxyurea (SCA-HU), or bone marrow transplant (SCA-BMT)
control_group_definition: SCA-SC group (supportive care, no HU or BMT)
Study Population: females with sickle cell anemia aged 10-21 years
Assay Method: Beckman-Coulter AMH Gen II enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA)
Experimental Method Details: Serum samples collected during routine clinic visit, centrifuged and stored; AMH measured by ELISA; low AMH defined as <5th percentile for age-matched controls

Evidence Quote: The AMH values were undetectable (b0.57 pmol/L) in all SCA-BMT subjects. Mean AMH levels were lower in the SCA-HU subjects as compared to the SCA-SC subjects but not statistically different (13.4 ± 15.4 pmol/L vs 17.1 ± 10.7 pmol/L; p = 0.41).

Title: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and telomere length predicts response to immunosuppressive therapy in pediatric aplastic anemia.

case_group_definition: children diagnosed with acquired aplastic anemia (age below 18 years, newly diagnosed disease ≤180 days without specific prior treatment, moderate to very severe symptoms)

Title: Red blood cells free α-haemoglobin pool: a biomarker to monitor the β-thalassemia intermedia variability. The ALPHAPOOL study.
Data_source_str: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT 02855957
case_group_definition: Patients with beta-thalassemia (different phenotypic expression) or alpha-thalassemia recruited at the Unité des Maladies Génétiques du Globule Rouge (UMGGR) of Henri Mondor Hospital
control_group_definition: Healthy volunteers recruited through the donor base of the hospital regardless of ethnic origin, without abnormalities of HBA1/HBA2 and HBB genes
Study Population: beta-thalassemia patients, alpha-thalassemia patients, and healthy controls
Assay Method: GST-AHSP binding assay with spectrophotometric quantification
Experimental Method Details: Haemolysates deposited on glutathione Sepharose 4B-coated 96-well filter plates with bound recombinant GST-AHSP, which traps free soluble alpha-Hb; quantity of alpha-Hb in eluted GST-AHSP/alpha-Hb complex and total Hb determined by spectrophotometry from the Soret band (414 nm); alpha-Hb pool expressed in ppm (ng alpha-Hb/mg total Hb subunits per ml haemolysate)
Clinical Outcome: discrimination between beta-thalassemia and non-beta-thalassemia subjects
Cutoff Value: 120 ng free alpha-Hb/mg of total Hb/ml of haemolysate (ppm)
Main Conclusion CN: α-Hb池测定可有效区分β-地中海贫血患者与对照及α-地中海贫血患者，可作为辅助诊断指标。
Evidence Quote: Receiver operator characteristic analyses revealed an area under the curve of 0±978 for the a-Hb pool measurement at a threshold of 120 ng free a-Hb/mg of total Hb/ml of haemolysate (ppm) with a sensitivity and speciﬁcity of 86% and 100%, respectively, to discriminate between b-thal and not b-thal subjects.

Title: Evidence for interactions between inflammatory markers and renin-angiotensin system molecules in the occurrence of albuminuria in children with sickle cell anemia.
Study Type: Cross-sectional study with a short-term prospective observational cohort subset
Data_source_str: Minas Gerais state cohort of children with sickle cell anemia followed at Fundação Hemominas outpatient clinic, Belo Horizonte, Brazil
case_group_definition: Children with sickle cell anemia and albuminuria (albumin/creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/g)
control_group_definition: Children with sickle cell anemia and normal albuminuria (albumin/creatinine ratio <30 mg/g), matched by age and sex
Experimental Method Details: Urinary levels measured using Human Chemokine Cytometric Bead Array Kit (BD Bioscience) and expressed as ratio to urine creatinine

Title: Interleukin-37 reduces inflammation and impairs phagocytosis of platelets in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP).

case_group_definition: Patients with ITP diagnosed according to 2011 American Society of Hematology guidelines, treatment-free at least 4 weeks prior to enrollment

Evidence Quote: Plasma IL-37 was significantly increased in ITP patients with platelet count lower than 30 × 109/L (median 163.50, interquartile range 263.70 pg/mL, n = 37) compared to healthy controls (median 95.30, interquartile range 116.87 pg/mL, n = 14, P = 0.0129), and ITP patients with platelet count above or equal to 30 × 109/L (median 63.26, interquartile range 37.89 pg/mL, n = 6, P = 0.0001; Fig. 1A).

Title: Pentraxin-3 is a candidate biomarker on the spectrum of severity from pre-eclampsia to HELLP syndrome: GenPE study.
Journal: Hypertension research : official journal of the Japanese Society of Hypertension
Data_source_str: GenPE study (Genetics and Pre-eclampsia), multicenter case-control study
race: Most women were of mixed ethnic ascendency
case_group_definition: Women with pre-eclampsia (blood pressure ≥140/90 mmHg on two separate occasions within a 24-h period and proteinuria ≥300 mg in 24 h or ≥1+ dipstick) or HELLP syndrome (PE with complete or incomplete pattern of hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and thrombocytopenia as defined by Sibai)
control_group_definition: Normotensive woman with an uneventful pregnancy delivering by labor or cesarean section at term (37–42 weeks)
Study Population: 1024 pregnant Colombian women (461 controls, 368 pre-eclampsia, 195 HELLP)

Comparison Groups: HELLP syndrome vs controls; pre-eclampsia vs controls
Clinical Outcome: Odds of HELLP syndrome per 1 ng/ml increase in PTX3 (fully adjusted)
Multivariable Result: Adjusted for maternal age, ethnicity, socioeconomic position, date and place of recruitment, family history of pre-eclampsia, smoking, BMI at beginning of pregnancy, gestational age and multiple pregnancy
Main Conclusion CN: 校正混杂因素后，PTX3每升高1 ng/ml，HELLP综合征风险增加（OR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08–1.18），关联强于子痫前期。
Evidence Quote: the strength of the association was higher for HELLP syndrome [OR 1.13 (95% CI 1.08; 1.18)] than for pre-eclampsia [OR 1.03 (95% CI 1.03; 1.10)]

Title: Complement activation as a biomarker for platelet-activating antibodies in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
Journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH
Data_source_str: patient plasma samples from Duke Coagulation Laboratory (2013-2022)
case_group_definition: Clinical HIT based on intermediate or high 4Ts score (4-6), positive anti-PF4/heparin IgG, and positive SRA
control_group_definition: Asymptomatic with anti-PF4/H antibodies (AAb+)
Study Population: patients with anti-PF4/H antibodies (HIT n=8, AAb+ n=14) and healthy donors (n=21)
Experimental Method Details: patient plasma added to healthy donor plasma with PF4/heparin, ULICs captured by KKO, detected with anti-C3c antibody
Comparison Groups: HIT vs AAb+ vs healthy donors
Clinical Outcome: discrimination of HIT from asymptomatic anti-PF4/H antibodies
P Value: p<0.0001 (HIT vs AAb+ or HD); p<0.01 (AAb+ vs HD)
Diagnostic Performance: ROC analysis: cut-off 1.825 sensitivity 1.0, specificity 0.929, 94.4% correct classification; cut-off 3.295 sensitivity 0.975, specificity 1.0, 95.4% correct classification; AUC 0.991
Main Conclusion CN: 补体激活（anti-C3c）在HIT患者中显著高于无症状抗PF4/H抗体患者，可作为鉴别致病性抗体的功能生物标志物。
Evidence Quote: plasmas from control subjects (Ab source) caused minimal activation of complement activation (mean anti-C3c A450nm ± SD), 0.288 ± 0.188, while AAb+ plasma caused greater complement activation than controls (0.748 ± 0.54; p<0.01). However, complement activation by HIT patient plasma was markedly higher than the other two cohorts (3.30 ± 0.608; p<0.0001 vs. AAb+ or HD, by one-way ANOVA).
